newsitem.title: USA: AMR, pilots exploring options - U.S. mediator.
newsitem.headline: AMR, pilots exploring options - U.S. mediator.

text.p: A federal mediator said on Tuesday that American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and its pilots had explored contract options but declined to say if any progress was made to avert a strike set for Friday midnight.

Kenneth Hipp, chairman of the National Mediation Board, told reporters the two sides had met until 10 p.m. EST Monday (0300 GMT Tuesday) and throughout Tuesday. They planned to meet into the night again Tuesday.
"I would characterize the talks thus far as a frank discussion of the issues and exploration of the options," Hipp said.
But, asked if progress was being made, he said, "We don't comment as to where we are in terms of the issues and how we are progressing." He referred reporters to the negotiating parties.
Hipp said the two sides may have their own views on whether any progress toward a settlement was being made.
"We remain hopeful of an early settlement (to avert the strike)," he said. The union has vowed to strike if no deal is reached.
The pilots want an 11.5 percent wage increase over the life of a four-year contract. American has offered five percent.
At issue also is American's plan to add jets to its regional carrier, American Eagle, and to use lower-paid pilots from another union to fly them. The APA wants its members in the cockpit.
An APA official said some progress had been made by the mere fact of meeting with mediators and American, but he said he had yet to see any real movement.

The official added, however, that an apparent AMR request to reopen some issues thought to have been settled in a provisional agreement late last year was counterproductive. The union wanted some clarification of the carrier's intent,t he official said.
There was no immediate comment from American.
